channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan Develops 2027-2030 Action Plan for Climate Change Adaptation
item.description: Tajikistan has finalized its National Adaptation Plan for Climate Change for 2027-2030. The plan, developed with UNDP and funded by the Green Climate Fund, includes 108 measures across 13 areas to reduce vulnerability to climate change impacts. Discussions also covered climate financing and capacity building.

item.title: Almaty Metro Extends Purchase of 10 New Electric Train Sets Until 2028
item.description: Almaty Metro plans to acquire 10 new electric train sets in phases over three years, with the first two expected in December 2026. The remaining trains will arrive in 2027 and 2028. Passenger traffic has increased significantly, with new station openings anticipated to further boost ridership.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's NAVBA Urges Enhanced Wallet Security After Binance Attack
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Agency for Virtual Assets and Blockchain Technologies (NAVBA) advises citizens to strengthen their crypto wallet security following a major cyberattack on Binance. NAVBA recommends two-factor authentication, strong passwords, and vigilance against phishing attempts to protect virtual assets.

item.title: Kazakh President's Address Discussed at Embassy Event in Moscow
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ambassador to Russia, Dauren Abayev, highlighted the significance of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address, 'Urgent Tasks of Kazakhstan in a New Historical Period.' The event in Moscow also noted the address's symbolic timing with Kazakhstan's 35th Independence anniversary. Russian officials praised the reformist direction and focus on developing institutions and infrastructure.

item.title: Almaty Court Orders Reconsideration of Afghan Citizen's Refugee Status Application
item.description: The Specialized Interdistrict Administrative Court of Almaty has ordered the Department of Employment and Social Programs to reconsider an Afghan citizen's application for refugee status due to new circumstances. This marks a unique case, as previous similar requests were denied. The applicant faced renewed threats upon returning to her homeland, prompting the legal action after her initial application was rejected.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Expanding Travel Between Turkic States Using ID Cards
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has proposed expanding the possibility of travel between Turkic states using only ID cards. He emphasized simplifying border crossing procedures and regulations for staying in host countries. This initiative aims to facilitate easier movement and enhance cooperation among member nations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Government Rejects Proposal for Single Simplified Tax Rate
item.description: The Kazakhstan government has stated it requires further assessment before supporting a proposal by deputies to introduce a single 2-3% tax rate for the simplified tax regime. The current Tax Code allows local authorities (maslikhats) to set rates between 2% and 6%, with many regions already implementing lower rates.

item.title: Kazakhstan Increases Primary Care Doctor Appointment Hours to Six Hours
item.description: Kazakhstan has extended the appointment hours for primary care doctors from four to six hours daily, aiming to improve access to healthcare. Waiting times have also been reduced to one to three days. The Ministry of Health reported these measures are being implemented nationwide to address shortcomings in appointment scheduling and patient access.

item.title: Auditor Testifies on Uncovering Embezzlement Scheme Involving Union Funds
item.description: An auditor detailed in an Almaty court how he uncovered a scheme to embezzle union funds. The scheme allegedly involved contracts with companies, one linked to the defendant's relative. The auditor, Medetbek Abdikalikov, a risk management manager, presented findings from his review of the union's financial documentation and contracts.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Introduce Drone Piloting Skills in School Military Training
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to integrate drone piloting skills into initial military training modules in schools as part of a comprehensive plan for unmanned systems development. The initiative includes establishing aviation modeling classrooms and equipping schools with specialized drone technology. The goal is to foster an engineering and operator elite from an early age.

item.title: Bishkek Overpass Cladding Damaged Months After Renovation
item.description: The recently renovated overpass at the intersection of Chingiz Aitmatov Avenue and Lev Tolstoy Street in Bishkek has suffered significant damage to its cladding. Large cracks and detached panels are visible, exposing the old stone surface. The repairs were completed just a few months ago, raising questions about material quality or installation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's government urged to increase funding for adult cancer treatment
item.description: A proposal has been made to allocate an additional 2 billion soms in the 2027 republican budget for the treatment of adult patients with oncological and hematological diseases. The head of the "Together Against Cancer" foundation stated that the real need for cancer treatment funding is around 9 billion soms.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev invites Russia to join the Organization of Turkic States as an observer
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has invited Russia to join the Organization of Turkic States as an observer, stating it would benefit all member countries. He made the proposal at the organization's 13th summit, emphasizing Russia's historical ties and the presence of Turkic peoples within its borders.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev: Turkic States Organization is not and should not become a military alliance
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated at the 13th summit of the Organization of Turkic States that the organization is not and should not become a military alliance. He emphasized strengthening the institutional structure and prioritizing key areas of cooperation, noting that some functions are duplicated. Tokayev also stressed the importance of adhering to signed agreements and creating a Council of Permanent Representatives.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev proposes expanding cooperation within the Turkic States Organization and inviting Russia
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed expanding cooperation within the Organization of Turkic States and inviting Russia. He highlighted the escalating global geopolitical situation and its impact on trade and logistics. Tokayev emphasized Kazakhstan's support for economic interaction within the organization, urging the swift adoption of the 2027-2031 strategy focused on concrete projects.

item.title: Turkey Assumes Chairmanship of the Organization of Turkic States
item.description: Turkey will now chair the Organization of Turkic States. At the summit, the Kazakh President urged a focus on institutional development and identifying priority areas, emphasizing that the organization is not and should not become a military alliance. He also highlighted the importance of establishing a Permanent Representatives Council.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Russia Join Organization of Turkic States as Observer
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed inviting Russia to join the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) as an observer or participate in the OTS+ format. He cited Russia's historical ties with the Turkic world and the presence of many Turkic peoples within its territory. This aligns with Kazakhstan's stance on the organization not being a military alliance.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev States Turkic States Organization is Not and Should Not Become a Military Alliance
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev declared at the Organization of Turkic States summit that it is not a military alliance and should not become one in the future, emphasizing this as Kazakhstan's position. He also proposed streamlining the organization's 60 current focus areas, noting some functions are redundant.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Total Internet Traffic Control and Roblox Ban
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering implementing total control over internet traffic and potentially blocking the gaming platform Roblox. Authorities also aim to restrict access to foreign online casinos and adult websites, as current measures are insufficient to block prohibited resources effectively, according to an official.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan Prime Ministers Discuss Bilateral Cooperation
item.description: The Prime Ministers of Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan, Adylbek Kasymaliyev and Olzhas Bektenov, met in Bishkek to discuss strengthening bilateral cooperation. They reviewed trade, investment, transport, water-energy, and cultural ties. The meeting also included the 14th session of the Kyrgyz-Kazakh Intergovernmental Council, focusing on implementing agreements between the two nations.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Urges Turkic States to Develop Middle Corridor and Digital Infrastructure
item.description: At the 13th summit of the Organization of Turkic States, Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev outlined priorities for cooperation in transport, digitalization, artificial intelligence, and culture. He called for accelerating the adoption of the Turkic States' strategy for 2027-2031, which includes developing trade, investment, and digital technologies. Tokayev also highlighted the Middle Corridor's growing importance, noting a 30% increase in transit traffic.

item.title: Four Men Convicted in Kazakhstan for Large-Scale Theft from Transit Trains
item.description: Four men have been convicted in Kazakhstan for stealing high-value electronics from transit cargo trains traveling from China to Western Europe. The group allegedly conspired to repeatedly break into containers carrying laptops and game consoles. In one incident in May 2025, 1,019 laptops were stolen from a train destined for Poland. The total material damage to companies exceeded $1.4 million.

item.title: Kazakhstan President: Digitalization and AI Development are Today's Imperatives
item.description: Kazakhstan's President stated that digitalization and artificial intelligence development are crucial today, emphasizing the country's goal to become a digital nation. He highlighted the establishment of an AI center, a university for AI specialists, data processing centers, and the adoption of a Digital Code and AI law. Kazakhstan is ready to share its experience with partner countries.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Investigator Arrested for Allegedly Demanding $1,200 Bribe
item.description: An investigator with Kyrgyzstan's State Penitentiary Service has been arrested in Bishkek on suspicion of extorting a bribe of 100,000 soms. The suspect was allegedly demanding the money for a favorable decision on a case. He was apprehended while receiving 60,000 soms and is currently held in pre-trial detention.

item.title: North Korea-Linked Hackers Suspected of Stealing $6.3 Billion from Binance
item.description: Hackers associated with North Korea are suspected of stealing $6.36 billion from the Binance cryptocurrency exchange, with a significant portion transferred in just 20 minutes. Analysis by TRM Labs suggests the involvement of the North Korean group TraderTraitor. This potential theft could be the largest in cryptocurrency history.

item.title: Kazakh President Calls for Swift Adoption of Turkic Cultural Heritage Convention
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev emphasized the importance of cultural and humanitarian cooperation at the 13th Summit of the Organization of Turkic States. He urged the swift adoption of a convention on preserving Turkic civilization's heritage and highlighted Kazakhstan's efforts in studying and promoting historical legacy, including a multi-volume history of Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Elderly Population Increased by 25% in Five Years, Study Shows
item.description: The number of elderly people in Kyrgyzstan has grown by 25% over the past five years, reaching approximately 737,000. This demographic shift necessitates a review of social policies and dedicated funding for elder support programs. Experts highlight the need for conditions promoting 'dignified longevity,' addressing age discrimination and social isolation.

item.title: Tokayev: Russia's Participation in OTS Would Be Right and Fair
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated at the 13th summit of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) that Russia's potential participation would be "right and fair." He highlighted the OTS as a unique structure strengthening Turkic unity and noted the summit's significance during the 100th anniversary of the first Turkology congress. Tokayev also addressed the escalating global geopolitical situation and its impact on trade and logistics.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Expanding Cooperation in AI and Digitalization within OTS
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has proposed expanding cooperation with Organization of Turkic States (OTS) countries in digitalization, artificial intelligence, and education. President Sadyr Japarov highlighted the potential for sharing experiences in digital public services and jointly developing new technologies, particularly AI in Turkic languages. He also emphasized leveraging Kyrgyzstan's High-Tech Park for joint innovation projects.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Proposes Russia Join Turkic States Organization as Observer
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev suggested Russia be granted observer status or join an expanded "Organization of Turkic States +" format. Speaking at the XIII summit, he stated this would strengthen cooperation, acknowledging Russia's historical ties to the Turkic world. Tokayev also addressed Middle East tensions and the need to structure the OTS's work.

item.title: 113 Migrants Arrive on Spanish Coast; Two, Including a Child, Died During Voyage
item.description: A small boat carrying 113 irregular migrants from Gambia arrived near El Hierro island, Spain. Rescuers found two deceased individuals, an adult male and a child, aboard the vessel. A critically ill infant was evacuated. Over 4,000 migrants have arrived in the Canary Islands this October alone.

item.title: Entrepreneurs' Cameras Allowed to Record Seatbelt Violations from November 1
item.description: A government decree permits entrepreneurs' photo and video recording devices to capture seatbelt violations starting November 1. These systems will now also record violations related to seatbelt usage.

item.title: Tajikistan National Bank and EBRD Discuss Financial Sector Development
item.description: The National Bank of Tajikistan and a delegation from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) met to discuss expanding cooperation, strengthening the financial system, improving the investment climate, and supporting the private sector. Special attention was given to insurance, financial literacy, sustainable financing, and green projects. They also explored risk distribution mechanisms to enhance lending and access to long-term financing for businesses.

item.title: Anadolu Group Plans to Launch Retail Chain in Uzbekistan Market
item.description: Turkey's Anadolu Group intends to enter the Uzbek market with its own retail chain, as discussed during a meeting between President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and the company's chairman. The group, which operates Turkey's Migros retail network, also explored establishing livestock complexes and meat/dairy production. Anadolu Group has previously invested in Coca-Cola İçecek and Anadolu Isuzu in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Pakistani Cleric Calls for International Investigation into Afghan Refugee Treatment
item.description: Maulana Fazlur Rehman, leader of Pakistan's JUI-F party, has urged international organizations to investigate the treatment of Afghan refugees in Pakistan. He cited reports of police raids and harassment, emphasizing the need for independent monitoring to protect refugees' rights and concerns amid ongoing humanitarian challenges.

item.title: Tajikistan President Inaugurates Pharmaceutical Plant and New Production Facilities in Dushanbe
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon has opened a new Tajik-Indian pharmaceutical plant, 'Razes Pharma,' in Dushanbe. The facility, equipped with international standard machinery, will initially produce 100 types of medicines, with plans to expand to 250. The plant will create over 300 jobs.

item.title: UNICEF: 12.7 Million Children Vaccinated Against Polio in Afghanistan
item.description: UNICEF reports that 12.7 million children in Afghanistan have been vaccinated against polio. Afghanistan remains one of two countries where wild poliovirus is endemic. Efforts to eradicate the disease continue, as the country has reported six new polio cases, bringing the total to 42 this year.

item.title: Tajikistan to Receive Over €72 Million for Climate Change Adaptation Projects
item.description: Tajikistan will receive over €72 million from the Green Climate Fund as part of a regional program for Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan. The funds are allocated for restoring forests and pastures, introducing new technologies, supporting farmers, and promoting sustainable agriculture. Uzbekistan will receive €103.75 million, and Kyrgyzstan €74.49 million.

item.title: Tajikistan and Qatar Discuss Joint Ventures in Free Economic Zones
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Economic Development and Trade met with the CEO of Qatar Free Zones Authority in Doha to discuss cooperation in free economic zones. The talks focused on investment opportunities, establishing joint enterprises, and collaboration in industrial production, agricultural processing, textiles, and construction materials.

item.title: Uzbekistan Paid Over 642 Billion Soums in Solar Energy Subsidies
item.description: In Uzbekistan, over 642 billion soums were paid in subsidies for solar energy. Over nine months, 70,700 citizens received state subsidies for solar energy fed into the power grid. The largest amounts were allocated to the regions of Bukhara, Khorezm, and the Republic of Karakalpakstan.
